evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:106-110 — ApiCallExecutor's reqwest::Client is built with only .timeout()/.user_agent() and NO .redirect(Policy::none()); reqwest defaults to following up to 10 redirects.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:251 — validate_external_url() runs ONCE on the initial URL only; the request is then issued at line 257-261 and sent at line 307 (request.send().await), which transparently follows 3xx redirects. A permitted external endpoint that responds 30x to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (or any internal 10.x/127.x host) is followed with NO re-validation of the hop target — SSRF bypass via redirect. The response body is then parsed and returned (line ~325), enabling exfiltration.

Reachability (traced end-to-end, hence confidence=high): services/actions/mod.rs registers ApiCallExecutor in the default ActionRegistry; services/workflow_executor.rs:275 tokio::spawns WorkflowExecutorTask.run which drives the registry against a tenant/admin-configured 'api_call' workflow action URL — an authenticated workflow author reaches this path in production.

Fix direction: set reqwest redirect Policy::none() (or a custom policy that re-runs validate_external_url on every hop and rejects internal targets); additionally resolve the host and validate every resolved IP, or pin the connection to the validated IP.
